instruction: Browse to the discussion forums and open the thread that contains the most responses from community members.

metadata.explanation: Task asks user to navigate to discussion forums and locate the thread with the highest response count. Validation confirms correct URL navigation.

llm_judge_reasons: Critical semantic gap: Instruction requires finding 'the thread that contains the most responses', but evaluator only checks if user navigated to a hardcoded URL without verifying it actually has the most responses
Cannot verify dynamic requirement: The thread with most responses can change over time as users add new responses, but evaluator uses static expected URL that assumes the answer never changes
Incomplete coverage: Evaluator does not verify that user actually compared response counts across threads or performed any search/comparison process - only checks final destination URL

Missing temporal validity: No mechanism to ensure the hardcoded expected URL (https://discussions.flightaware.com/t/the-banter-thread/4412) still represents the thread with most responses at evaluation time
Logic flaw: Task is fundamentally about comparison (finding maximum), but evaluator performs no comparison logic - just URL matching
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Use get_info_from_website to dynamically extract response counts from multiple threads in the discussion forum at evaluation time, then verify the opened thread has the maximum count
Add get_active_tab_html_parse to extract response count from the current thread page, then compare against known thread counts or verify it matches a dynamically-determined maximum

Modify expected value to include response count verification: expected should specify both the URL pattern AND that the response count is greater than a threshold or is the maximum among listed threads
Add metadata explaining when the expected URL was determined and what the response count was at that time, so temporal validity can be assessed
Consider changing instruction to be less dynamic (e.g., 'Open the Banter Thread in discussions') OR make evaluator truly dynamic by querying forum state at runtime
